clue.text: Get up and fight for your principles

definitions.meaning: to rise to your feet, stand up
to adopt a firm position and defend it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the phrase: physically getting onto your feet, and figuratively holding firm on an issue.

clue.text: Help someone to have a flutter on the gee-gees

definitions.meaning: to assist or encourage a person, often in wrongdoing

definitions.text: to have a flutter on the gee-gees
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a wager on the horses

explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist a person; split in two it reads as a single wager, a flutter on horses (gee-gees is British slang for racehorses).

clue.text: Archdeacon appears in cathedral city with regularity

indicators.note: the churchman shows up inside the city, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Ely is the Cambridgeshire cathedral city
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman turns up regularly in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is formally addressed as the Venerable; Ely is a small Cambridgeshire city with a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a steady, uniform way is doing it with regularity.

clue.text: They ridicule capture of flag by life army regiment

indicators.note: the regiment holds the other word captive, so it goes inside

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service regiment
to flag is to tire, grow weary

explanation.surface: Lampoons mock a crack regiment for seizing an enemy banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life' is likely an OCR slip for 'elite'. 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning grow weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Satires are works that mock their targets, so they ridicule.

clue.text: Article by Mr Dawson on alcoholic drinks

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
Les Dawson was a British comedian

explanation.surface: A piece written about a comedian's drinking habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Dawson was a well-known British TV comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, a common kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Desmond isn't able to sing treble

parts.note: Des is the short form of the name Desmond
can't means is not able

explanation.surface: A man called Desmond cannot hit the high notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a high melody sung above the tune, the treble line.

clue.text: A theologian is given a couple of degrees in Ethiopia

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, denotes a theologian

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the degree is written twice

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A religious scholar is awarded two qualifications in Ethiopia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. BA is written twice for the couple of degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia, so it is found there.

clue.text: Panorama journalist looked for mine

parts.note: a prospect is a wide view, a panorama
ed, short for editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A TV reporter on Panorama investigated a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC current affairs programme, but here it just means a view.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectors search for gold or minerals, so they look for a mine.

clue.text: Acting academy returning from a month in Israel

indicators.note: coming back, so the drama school's letters run backwards

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London

explanation.surface: A drama student comes home from a month spent in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses RADA, the London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is a month of the Jewish calendar, observed in Israel.

clue.text: Cruel advice to those who forgive too readily

definitions.meaning: merciless, pitiless

definitions.text: advice to those who forgive too readily
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a tip to soften less often

explanation.definitionFit: Relentless means unyielding and harsh; split in two it tells the soft-hearted to give in less.

clue.text: Worries about one form of dental decay

indicators.note: the worries go around the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: cares are worries
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a particular kind of tooth decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the dentist's word for tooth decay, cavities.

clue.text: It imposes infantile restriction on writer of drama

parts.note: a play is a drama
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A censor limits a playwright's childish work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer of drama' wants to be a playwright; it is the pen for the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is an enclosure that confines a baby or toddler.

clue.text: Local haunt for the ceramicist in Hertfordshire

parts.note: a potter is a ceramicist; the possessive gives the final S
a bar is a pub or local

explanation.surface: A pottery maker's regular drinking place in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar is a town in Hertfordshire, just north of London; 'local' is British for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Potters Bar lies in the county of Hertfordshire.

clue.text: Review of bare allowance represented a deviation

indicators.note: a review re-examines and reworks, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Reassessing a meagre allowance was an unusual departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review of' rearranges BARE into ABER; 'represented' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from what is normal, a deviation.

clue.text: Polly Peck's founder in the depths of despair

definitions.meaning: Asil ... founded the Polly Peck business empire
the lowest point

explanation.definitionFit: Asil Nadir ran the collapsed Polly Peck group; the common noun means the lowest point, rock bottom.

clue.text: Working actors are travelling by coach

definitions.meaning: performers at work are in front of the audience
a passenger on a stagecoach rides on it

explanation.definitionFit: Performers at work stand before an audience; travellers ride aboard a horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: Where the sprinkler is kept to hand

definitions.meaning: a garden sprinkler is attached to the faucet
readily available

explanation.definitionFit: A sprinkler fixed to a faucet is literally attached there; figuratively the phrase means readily available.

clue.text: Templar provides subject matter for hagiography

definitions.meaning: Simon Templar is the fictional hero known by this nickname
a hagiography is a holy person's biography

explanation.definitionFit: Simon Templar's nickname is The Saint; hagiographies are biographies of holy figures.

clue.text: You must note difference between fianc and fiance

definitions.meaning: an old form of you, the familiar object pronoun
the print lost its accents: the feminine French form adds one extra letter E

explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text dropped the accented letters; the setter's words were fiancé and fiancée, which differ by one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is archaic second-person usage; the two French words differ only by an extra E.

clue.text: Speedy way to dispose of spare tyre

definitions.meaning: quick

definitions.text: way to dispose of spare tyre
definitions.meaning: going without food loses belly fat

explanation.definitionFit: Speedy means quick; going without food is a way to lose a roll of belly fat.

clue.text: Self-righteous act put on by Indian restaurateur

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious
an act of Parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A curry-house owner puts on a sanctimonious performance.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is British slang for sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaw is a spiced rice dish an Indian restaurant serves up.

clue.text: Aristocrats of the same generation

definitions.meaning: the body of nobles
read as two words, an equal's time of life

explanation.definitionFit: The lords of the realm form a body; split, the word gives an equal and an era of life.

clue.text: Clothes-press for Welsh campanologist

parts.note: a campanologist is a bell-ringer

explanation.surface: A mangle belonging to a bell-ringer from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A wringer is a mangle that squeezes water out of washing.

clue.text: Former nobleman and I presented to Her Majesty

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
ER is the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A former peer and the speaker are introduced to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented to' is a link; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means previous, prior, in the sense former.

clue.text: Rewarded in advance for help with homework

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework
aid means help

explanation.surface: A pupil is paid upfront for assistance with their homework.
explanation.walkthrough: PREP is a British school word for homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepaid means paid beforehand, so rewarded ahead of time.

clue.text: Walk around the Italian bishop's residence

indicators.note: the walking word goes round the article, enclosing it

parts.note: to pace is to walk
la is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Strolling round the Italian bishop's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's official home is called his palace.

clue.text: Model of no standing at all

definitions.meaning: a person who poses for a portrait
one who is seated rather than upright

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model poses, often seated; a seated person is literally not standing.

clue.text: Put clothes about a child

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
a lad is a boy, a child

explanation.surface: Dressing a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is the past participle of clothe, describing one who has put clothes on.

clue.text: Blemish found on second automobile

parts.note: a car is an automobile

explanation.surface: A dent found on a second vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on skin, a blemish.

clue.text: Loyalty, for instance, is required in international agreement

indicators.note: the example abbreviation is needed inside the treaty word, so it goes within

parts.note: an alliance is a pact between nations
eg means for example

explanation.surface: Fidelity, for example, is needed in a treaty between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithfulness owed to a cause or ruler.

clue.text: I feel all right, despite murderous rage

parts.note: I am, said of how one feels
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone claims to feel fine despite being in a killing fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I feel all right' becomes I AM OK, the I dropped. 'despite' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok is a frenzied violent rampage, from a Malay word.

clue.text: Presbyter gets soft fruit to make wine

parts.note: an elder is a presbyter in some churches
a berry is a soft fruit

explanation.surface: A church elder gathers fruit for home brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderberries are the dark fruit of the elder tree, a classic country-wine ingredient.
